# Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**4:1** And-I-returned [ve-shavti], I, and-I-saw all the-oppressions [ha-ashuqim] that are-done under the-sun: and-behold, the-tears [dim'at] of-the-oppressed [ha-ashuqim], and-there-is-no [ein] comforter [menachem] for-them; and-from-the-hand of-their-oppressors [osheqeihem] [was] power [ko'ach], and-there-is-no comforter for-them.

**4:2** And-I-praised [ve-shabbe'ach ani] the-dead [ha-metim] who already have-died [she-kevar metu] more-than the-living [ha-chayyim] who are still alive [adennah chayyim]. **4:3** And-better [tov] than-both-of-them [mi-sheneihem] [is] he-who has-not-yet [adennah lo] been [hayah], who has-not-seen the-evil work [ha-ma'aseh ha-ra] that-is-done under the-sun.

**4:4** And-I-saw, I, all the-toil [ha-amal] and all the-skill [kishron] of-the-work [ha-ma'aseh], that it [is] the-envy [qin'at] of-a-man from-his-neighbor [me-re'ehu]. Also this [is] vapor [havel] and-striving-after wind.

**4:5** The-fool [ha-kesil] folds [chobeq] his-hands [et-yadav] and-eats his-own-flesh [et-besaro]. **4:6** Better [tov] [is] a-handful [melo khaf] of-rest [nachat] than-two-handfuls [mi-melo chofnayim] of-toil [amal] and-striving-after wind.

**4:7** And-I-returned, I, and-I-saw vapor under the-sun: **4:8** There-is one [echad] and-there-is-no second [sheni] — also a-son or-a-brother there-is-not to-him — and-there-is-no end [ein sof] to-all his-toil, and-also his-eye [eino] is-not satisfied [lo tisba] with-riches [osher]. "And-for-whom am-I toiling and-depriving [mechasseir] my-soul [nafsho] of-good [mi-tovah]?" Also this [is] vapor and-an-evil [ra] task [inyan] it [is].

**4:9** Better [tovim] [are] the-two [ha-shenayim] than the-one [ha-echad], for there-is to-them a-good reward [sakhar tov] in-their-toil. **4:10** For if they-fall [yippolu], the-one will-raise [yaqim] his-companion [et-chavero]; but-woe [ve-ilo] to-the-one [la-echad] who-falls and-there-is-no second [sheni] to-raise-him.

**4:11** Also if two lie-down [yishkevu], it-is-warm [ve-cham] to-them; but-the-one [la-echad] — how can-he-be-warm [eikh yecham]? **4:12** And-if one-overpowers-him [yitqefo ha-echad], the-two will-stand [ya'amdu] against-him [negdo]; and-the-threefold [ha-meshullash] cord [ha-chut] is-not quickly [bi-meherah] broken [yinnataq].

**4:13** Better [tov] [is] a-youth [yeled] poor [misken] and-wise [ve-chakham] than a-king old [zaqen] and-foolish [u-kesil], who does-not-know [lo yada] to-be-warned [le-hizzaher] anymore [od].

**4:14** For from-the-house of-prisoners [mi-beit ha-surim] he-came-out [yatza] to-reign [li-melokh], for also in-his-kingdom [be-malkhuto] he-was-born [nolad] poor [rash]. **4:15** I-saw all the-living [ha-chayyim] who-walk [ha-mehallekhim] under the-sun with the-youth [ha-yeled], the-second [ha-sheni], who stands [ya'amod] in-his-place [tachtav]. **4:16** There-is-no end [ein sof] to-all the-people [ha-am], to-all who were before-them [li-feneihem]; also the-latter-ones [ha-acharonim] will-not rejoice [lo yismechu] in-him. For also this [is] vapor and-striving-after wind.

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "there is no comforter":** The phrase *ein lahem menachem* occurs twice in this verse — a rare, emphatic repetition. The oppressed have no comfort, and even the observer (Qohelet) cannot provide it. This doubles the weight of the observation.

**v.12 — "the threefold cord":** The Hebrew *ha-chut ha-meshullash* is often quoted out of context. In context, it concludes a practical argument about companionship: one is vulnerable, two are better, three are best. The image is of rope — braided strands resist breaking.

**v.5-6 — A proverb pair:** These two proverbs seem to contradict each other. The fool does nothing (folds his hands); but two handfuls of striving is also foolish. Qohelet's wisdom sits between laziness and overwork.

*-- EMET*
